subject: math
cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane

items.prompt:
Which is an undefined term in geometry?
A) Segment
B) Point
C) Angle
D) Triangle

steps: Point is one of the three undefined terms.

items.prompt:
Two lines that meet at a right angle are:
A) Parallel
B) Perpendicular
C) Skew
D) Equal

A circle is the set of all points a fixed distance from a:
A) Line
B) Vertex
C) Center
D) Ray

steps: Every point of a circle is the radius distance from its center.

items.prompt:
An angle is formed by:
A) Two parallel lines
B) Two rays with a common endpoint
C) Three points
D) A single line
items.answer: B) Two rays with a common endpoint

steps: Two rays sharing an endpoint form an angle.

items.prompt:
Which figure has exactly two endpoints?
A) A line
B) A ray
C) A line segment
D) A plane

steps: A segment is bounded by two endpoints.

items.prompt:
Two coplanar lines that never intersect are:
A) Perpendicular
B) Parallel
C) Rays
D) Angles

steps: Same-plane lines that never meet are parallel.

items.prompt:
Why must geometry begin with undefined terms such as point and line?
A) Because they are unimportant
B) Because every definition rests on simpler terms, and some starting terms cannot be defined further
C) Because they have no use
D) Because they are the same thing
items.answer: B) Because every definition rests on simpler terms, and some starting terms cannot be defined further

steps: Definitions must rest on undefined basic terms.

items.prompt:
Opposite rays from a common endpoint form an angle measuring:
A) $45°$
B) $90°$
C) $180°$
D) $360°$

steps: Opposite rays form a straight angle of $180°$.
